messages:
Maya: FYI I opened a PR to harmonize several terms across the migration guide and SDK snippets. Main swaps: 'serving runtime' -> 'inference runtime', 'instance' -> 'replica' in examples, and consistent mention of 'Dedicated' (capital D) for the product. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/512
Jordan: nice. question: are we deliberately capitalizing Dedicated everywhere? marketing pages use 'dedicated capacity' lowercase. we should align with product naming (Dedicated is the product tier)
Ellen: agree with Jordan. product team confirmed the proper nouns: 'Redwood Dedicated' (capitalized) and 'dedicated capacity' (lowercase) when used generically. let's add a style rule.
Kevin: +1. on 'inference runtime' vs 'serving runtime' — which is preferred? infra folks still say serving runtime in engineering docs.
Maya: proposal: use 'inference runtime' in user-facing docs and quickstarts, keep 'serving runtime' in architecture deep dives. add glossary entries that cross-reference both.
Jordan: sounds pragmatic. can you add an alias in the glossary: "inference runtime (aka serving runtime)" so search catches both?
Ellen: also spotted inconsistent use in SDK snippets: some examples use 'ReplicaCount' (PascalCase), others 'replica_count' (snake). We should decide per-language: JS/TS use camelCase, Python use snake_case, CLI examples kebab-case. I'll add a checklist item to the PR to normalize per-language.
docs-bot: reminder: glossary.yml currently has an entry for 'runtime' but no explicit anchors for cross-refs. created issue #878 to add redirect anchors.
Maya: added small in-PR note: "style followups: normalize param casing in SDK examples (separate PRs per language), add glossary anchors (issue #878)"
Kevin: minor phrasing nit: in the migration guide we say "pin model version" vs "pin a model version". prefer the latter for clarity. I'll push a one-line patch.
Maya: pushed the patch. also switched example model handle to kebab-case in code blocks to match CLI examples.
Jordan: LGTM. can we add a single sentence in the style guide page: "Prefer 'inference runtime' for user docs; use 'serving runtime' in infra/architecture docs" so future writers have guidance?
Ellen: I'll PR that into docs/style/terminology after this merges.
Maya: ok moving to reviewers. thanks all :rocket:
